subject: Deal bridge: GPU holdback request (Osprey AI)
messages:
From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@ospreyai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity confirmation for Q3 production

Alex —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Osprey AI is on a fast track to a Q3 production launch and procurement asked me to get a short written confirmation of capacity availability and a request to lock a small slice of dedicated GPU capacity while we finish internal approvals.

High level ask:
- Target start: 2028-07-01
- Expected steady-state: 8x A100-like GPUs (24/7) for inference + burst pool of 12 GPUs for retraining windows (4–6 hours / day)
- Initial commit window: 12 months

We can share the draft PO and a short SOW. We need a provisional hold on the required fleet by end of next week to avoid being queued behind a few other Q3 deals. Can you confirm whether Redwood can put a soft hold and what the process/lead time looks like to convert into a firm reserved allocation?

Attaching PO draft for context.

Appreciate a quick confirm — even an informal "can do" is helpful for my procurement team.

Thanks,
Liam Carter
VP Product
Osprey AI
Attachments: Osprey-PO-draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam Carter <liam.carter@ospreyai.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity confirmation for Q3 production

Team — forwarding a request from a late-stage prospect (Osprey). They want a provisional hold on capacity while procurement completes the PO. Can Ops confirm whether we have the spare headroom and what the timeline is to convert a soft hold into a reserved Dedicated allocation?

Quick context: deal id OP-2147, likely committed ARR but procurement runs a 2–3 week review. They want to avoid being queued for Q3 capacity.

Please reply with:
- current available GPUs (region-us) that could satisfy 8 steady + 12 burst
- suggested hold model (soft tag vs provisional reservation) and how to tag it in the system
- dependencies (finance approval, SOC checklist, network/VPC prep)

I marked this high priority — they said they need an informal confirmation by EOW.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam Carter <liam.carter@ospreyai.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity confirmation for Q3 production

Alex —

Short answer: yes, we can accommodate a provisional hold for OP-2147. Summary of internal availability (us region, current snapshot):
- Total unallocated A100-equivalent capacity: 56 GPUs
- Fragmentation note: 8 GPUs are reserved for an internal POC window (2028-06-20 to 2028-07-05) but can be scheduled if needed
- Burst: we can guarantee a 12-GPU burst pool with a preemption policy (non-guaranteed during major infra events)

Recommended approach:
1) Soft hold (Sales Ops tag): place a timeboxed soft tag for 14 days that prevents the capacity from being offered to new committed deals. This requires approval from Finance to accept a pending PO as a valid hold reason.
2) Operational steps: Sales Ops creates a provisional allocation ticket in the capacity tracker and assigns a TTL (14 days). Engineering tags the capacity as "soft-hold-OP-2147".
3) Conversion: once PO signed + payment/commit confirmed, escalate to Dedicated provisioning to flip the soft hold into a reserved allocation (this requires a billing commit and change to autoscaling policy).

Dependencies / blockers:
- Finance confirmation on accepting a 14-day soft hold (we need them looped)
- SOC 2 onboarding checklist: Osprey has completed the high-level questionnaire but we need an expected date for evidence (they indicated 4–6 business days)
- Network/VPC prep: infra team needs a lead time of ~7 business days after reservation to prep VPC peering and IAM rules

I attached a quick capacity snapshot and a minimal checklist. If Sales wants, I can place the soft hold immediately after Finance gives the nod.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
Attachments: q3-capacity-plan-osprey.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Liam Carter <liam.carter@ospreyai.com>, procurement@ospreyai.com
Date: Mon, 21 Apr 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity confirmation for Q3 production

Thanks Vivek — good summary. Finance OK to accept a 14-day soft hold when Sales Ops attaches the draft PO and HubSpot deal record. Action items:

1) Alex: please create a Sales Ops ticket with the draft PO and link to HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345). Include expected start date 2028-07-01 and the OP-2147 tag.
2) Vivek/Eng: place the "soft-hold-OP-2147" tag against 8 steady GPUs + 12 burst in the us-primary cluster. TTL = 14 days.
3) Alex/Sales: get signed PO into DocuSign by EOW or notify if timing slips (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/OP-2147).

Once PO is signed and payment term on file, Sales Ops will convert the soft hold into a reserved allocation and update billing. Engineering to run the VPC prep checklist (7 business days lead) once the reservation is firm.

I'm authorizing the soft hold now — Vivek, please confirm when the capacity is tagged so Alex can report back to Osprey.

Karthik Iyer
VP Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
